title: Console API: route-level quantization settings endpoints (RBAC + audit log)
author: Chloe Martin
description:
Adds the control-plane API endpoints used by Console to read/write route-level quantization settings (enable/disable, canary percent, and optional pinned profile selector), including RBAC enforcement and audit log events.

Context: The Quantization Profile Library is opt-in and route-scoped. Console needs a stable API surface to (a) show current effective settings and (b) update settings safely with validation + auditing.

What’s in this PR: 1) New endpoints (internal/control-plane) GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/routes/{route_id}/quantization-settings and PUT /v1/orgs/{org_id}/routes/{route_id}/quantization-settings; 2) RBAC: requires route:read for GET and route:write + quantization:manage for PUT (enforced server-side; no trust in Console); 3) Audit log: emits event route.quantization_settings.updated with before/after and actor context; 4) Validation rules: canary_percent must be 0..100; enabling quantization requires canary_percent > 0 OR explicit enabled=true with canary_percent defaulting to 100 (Console will set explicitly); profile_selector supports "auto" (runtime resolves best compatible profile) or "pinned:<profile_id>@<version>"; reject pinned selectors that reference unknown profiles; 5) Optimistic concurrency: supports If-Match with settings_etag; responds 409 on mismatch; 6) Tests: unit tests for policy/RBAC gates, validation, audit payload redaction, and end-to-end handler tests through router.

Notes/decisions: - These endpoints store route-level intent only; precedence resolution (org vs customer vs route) continues to happen in the policy engine. The response includes both "configured" and "effective" view so Console can render why a route is running baseline vs quantized. - Audit payload includes profile selector string but omits any customer secrets; actor identity is taken from auth context and includes service principals.

Rollout: gated behind feature flag console_quantization_route_settings_api; Console will start reading the GET endpoint first (read-only rollout), then writing in a follow-up once UX is ready.

Screenshots: n/a (API-only).

Risk: Low/medium. Primary risk is misconfigured RBAC leading to unauthorized toggles; mitigated via explicit permission checks + audit logging + integration tests.

Follow-ups: - Add support for customer-level overrides in the same resource path once precedence model is finalized (tracked in ENG-18503 for rollback automation hooks + PM follow-up). - Wire these settings into route settings export/import tooling (future).
commits: control-plane: add quantization route settings model + etag support
api: implement GET/PUT route quantization settings endpoints
rbac: require quantization:manage for write operations
audit: emit route.quantization_settings.updated with before/after diff
tests: handler + rbac + validation coverage for quant settings endpoints
docs(internal): update console api index for quantization settings routes
conversation: Dylan Brooks (review): Can you clarify the response shape for Console? We’ll need both the configured route setting and what’s actually effective after precedence/fallback. Also, please avoid adding another ad-hoc endpoint without OpenAPI updates.

Chloe Martin (author): Yep — updated handler to return {configured, effective, effective_source}. configured is the stored route intent; effective is the resolved view after policy precedence. Also added OpenAPI entries in console_internal.yaml and a small internal doc note.

Jordan Lee (review): RBAC: route:write is not sufficient to toggle quantization. We should require an explicit quantization permission so only a smaller set of admins can flip it org-wide. Please also ensure service principals are attributed in audit logs.

Chloe Martin (author): Agreed. Added quantization:manage requirement for PUT, in addition to route:write. Audit actor now captures both user and service principal IDs from auth context; tests added for both paths.

Marcus Lin (security review): For audit payloads, do not log raw headers or auth tokens. Also, make sure pinned profile selectors are validated against the registry and that errors don’t leak internal registry URLs.

Chloe Martin (author): Confirmed. Audit payload logs only the selector string + numeric canary percent + enabled state; no headers. Pinned selectors are validated via registry client; errors are mapped to a generic 400 with a stable error code (QUANT_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND) and no internal URLs.

Priya Natarajan (review): The If-Match behavior is good, but can we return the new ETag on successful PUT so Console can do a clean read-modify-write? Also, what’s the default canary behavior if enabled is true but percent omitted?

Chloe Martin (author): Added ETag header on both GET and PUT responses. For defaults, server now requires Console to send canary_percent explicitly when enabled=true; otherwise 400 (CANARY_REQUIRED). This prevents accidental 100% rollouts due to client omission. Console UX will set 0/10/50/100 explicitly.

Benji Okafor (review): Nit: please align error semantics with our API conventions (use error_code + message, and 409 for etag mismatch). Also add a metric for write attempts denied by RBAC so SRE can catch misconfigured roles.
Chloe Martin (author): Done. Error shape standardized and 409 on ETag mismatch. Added metric controlplane.rbac.denied tagged with endpoint + required_permission.

Dylan Brooks (review): Looks good now. One last request: can we include a field that indicates whether quantization is globally disabled for the org (so the UI can show why the route toggle is inert)?

Chloe Martin (author): Added effective_source = ORG_DISABLED when org-level policy disables quantization; effective.enabled will be false in that case. Console can display a callout. Added a test case.
Marcus Lin (security review): Approved with the audit payload change; thanks.
Dylan Brooks (review): Approved. Please ensure feature flag is default-off in prod until Console is ready.
Chloe Martin (author): Flag is default-off; added note in rollout section and config default.
